best_lineage.idea: Parallelize over row blocks with std::thread using all available hardware cores (bounded to 10), since n=1024 gives enough work per thread to amortize launch overhead and the i-k-j order lets each thread stream contiguous B rows and C rows.

Add cache blocking over k (and i/j tiles) to the existing row-parallel i-k-j NEON kernel so A rows and B panels stay in L2/L1 and reuse C rows across multiple k blocks, improving memory locality for large n without changing the correct C-zeroing and accumulation semantics.

Switch from per-row k-blocking to full i-k-j cache blocking with B-panel packing: each thread processes row tiles, and for each k tile it packs the B tile rows into a contiguous panel so the inner j loop streams contiguous memory while reusing loaded A values from registers.
